text: The leak is understood: every trailing-window feature needs one fixed OBSERVATION_DATE per row, not a date that depends on whether the account later churned.
logins_last_30d, logins_last_90d, open_support_tickets_last_90d, and days_since_last_login all get rebuilt relative to that single fixed date, strictly excluding anything that happened after it.
The label comes from a separate, independent forward-looking window -- churn strictly after OBSERVATION_DATE and within the next 90 days -- never touching the features.
LightGBM gets retrained on the corrected features, and the same honest backtest now lands at about 0.79 -- a real, believable lift over the 0.74 honest baseline.
A new standing rule closes the gap for good: every trailing-window feature gets checked against one question before it ships.
